title: Incident Prioritization & SIEM Ingest Guidance
summary: Practical on-call guidance to prioritize RBAC and audit-log signals, standardize SIEM ingestion fields, and capture automatable evidence for faster containment and cleaner postmortems.
content:
Purpose:
This note is a pragmatic checklist and decision guide for security oncall responders when faced with RBAC anomalies, audit-log gaps, or SIEM ingestion issues. It focuses on fast prioritization, what evidence to collect automatically vs. manually, and how to normalize fields for reliable correlation in the SIEM. Use this as a lightweight runbook during incidents and as a reference for engineers who implement ingestion pipelines or evidence-automation hooks.

Audience and scope:
- Primary: security oncall, SRE/security platform engineers, incident commanders.
- Scope: RBAC v2 drift, unexpected role grants, service principal key use, suspicious privilege escalations, missing audit events, SIEM ingest backfills. Not a replacement for full IR playbooks — this is a rapid triage + ingestion checklist.

Quick prioritization matrix (one-page mental model):
- Severity S0 (urgent): active privilege escalation in prod that can cause data exfil, or mass role grants to wildcard principals. Immediate containment and exec page.
- Severity S1 (high): anomalous service account key creation in prod, or repeated failed privilege validation across many services. Oncall + incident lead.
- Severity S2 (medium): single-user suspicious access attempts of sensitive resources, or delayed audit exports > 6 hours. Monitor and investigate.
- Severity S3 (low): minor SIEM parser errors, non-prod RBAC experiments, or stale role descriptions. Triage in squad backlog.

Initial 10-minute checklist for first responder:
1) Confirm signal: copy the original alert (alert id, SIEM link, rule name).
2) Identify scope: impacted principal(s), target resource(s), timestamp range for suspicious activity.
3) Containment: if S0/S1, rotate affected keys, block principal in edge ACL, or activate pre-approved fallback role.
4) Evidence harvest (automated first): trigger evidence-automation pipeline to pull canonical audit events for the time window. Save raw audit bundle and normalized events to evidence storage.
5) Note communication: post short incident summary to #security-oncall with severity, short scope, and incident lead.
6) Start decision log (see template below).

Decision log template (paste into incident doc):
- Incident id: (auto-generated)
- First seen: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC
- Reporter: (alert source / person)
- Severity assigned: S0/S1/S2/S3
- Key decisions & times: (e.g., 14:12 rotate key; 14:18 blocked ip-range)
- Evidence artifacts (IDs/paths): (audit-bundle-20251112-1412.tar.gz, siem-case-9876)
- Follow-ups assigned: (owner, ETA)

Audit log schema guidance for SIEM ingest (recommended canonical fields):
- event_id: unique audit event id (string)
- event_timestamp: ISO8601 UTC timestamp
- actor_principal: login or service account id that performed the action
- actor_type: user | service_account | api_key | unknown
- action: high-level action verb (grant_role | remove_role | create_key | authenticate | access_resource)
- resource: resource path or id (project:/db/table, cluster:/namespace)
- resource_type: iam_role | secret | container | dataset | instance
- outcome: success | failure | denied | error
- request_id: request trace id from infra (if available)
- audit_schema_version: v2 (include schema version for parsing compatibility)

Notes on mapping and tagging: avoid free-text blobs for the crucial fields above. The SIEM should index event_timestamp, actor_principal, action, resource, outcome, and audit_schema_version. Add tags: environment:prod/stage/dev, region, and detection_rule_ids.

Common RBAC signal patterns to prioritize:
- mass-grant: more than N grant_role events within T minutes for the same grantor (possible automation bug or attack).
- service-account-key-create-in-prod: immediate S1 unless linked to approved job rollout.
- cross-project-role-bind: unexpected binding where external-principal is granted org-level access.
- permission-escalation-chain: sequence of lower-privilege CRUD leading to grant_role events.

Evidence automation checkpoints (what to automate now):
- Pull raw audit events for the 15 minutes before and after the alert timestamp.
- Snapshot IAM bindings and effective policy for affected resources (store JSON).
- Export associated login and access tokens metadata (IP, user-agent, MFA status) where available.
- Capture any existing cached KV (prefix cache) identifiers referenced by the audit event to aid replay.
- Lock the export with immutable storage retention tag and cryptographic hash to preserve chain of custody.

When automation fails (common causes listed):
- Missing API access credentials for the automation account: escalate to platform infra oncall.
- Audit export lag > 30 minutes: mark as S1 and start manual evidence pulls via cloud console/cli.
- Partial events (no actor_id): attempt enrichment with trace id and request logs; if not possible, treat as medium-priority and document gaps.

SIEM ingest troubleshooting tips:
- Parser mismatch: check audit_schema_version. If version mismatch, do not drop events — route to a "quarantine" index with raw payload for manual parsing.
- Time skew: normalize event_timestamp to server-side ingestion time and store original timestamp in event_timestamp_raw field.
- Duplicates: use event_id as dedupe key. If event_id missing, synthesize a stable key combination (actor+action+resource+timestamp).

Containment play examples (concise):
- Compromised service account key in prod (S1/S0): rotate keys, disable job queues referencing that key, and revert to last known-good deployment.
- Mass role grant from CI system (S1): disable CI token that performed grants, rollback recent pipeline changes, and re-run pipeline in audit-only mode.
- Unexpected org-level binding (S0): remove binding, add temporary explicit deny rule for external principals, open emergency change request with infra to prevent immediate reapply.

Post-incident evidence checklist (for postmortem):
- Archive raw audit bundle, normalized SIEM events, and chain-of-custody hashes.
- Save final decision log and timelines.
- Record what evidence was missing and why (ingest gap, permission error, schema drift).
- Concrete remediation actions (short-term and long-term) assigned to owners with target dates.

Implementation notes for platform/ingest engineers (practical):
- Prefer newline-delimited JSON for audit export. Include a top-level audit_schema_version.
- Tag every event with an ingestion_source and ingestion_received_at to diagnose pipeline delays.
- Ensure the automation role can only read audit logs and write to the evidence bucket; separation prevents accidental changes.

Open questions and follow-ups (work-in-progress):
- Threshold tuning: what values of N/T for mass-grant are reasonable across prod workloads? (action: run 30-day retrospective to propose thresholds).
- Evidence retention policy: current S3 lifecycle might purge older bundles — need to align with legal hold window.
- Conflation of action names across services: create a crosswalk doc to map service-specific verbs to canonical action values.

Quick references and links:
- Confluence: SIEM Field Map (linked)
- Jira: JIRA-SEC-4123 (automation pipeline backlog)
- Slack: #security-oncall for real-time coordination

Notes to self and next edits: add sample curl/cli snippets for manual audit pulls, and include a brief flow diagram. Also solicit input from platform team on immutable evidence tagging scheme.

Appendix: short manual audit pull commands (examples)
- gcloud: gcloud logging read "resource.type=audited_resource AND timestamp>\"2025-11-12T14:00:00Z\"" --limit 1000 --format json > audit-window.json
- aws: aws cloudtrail lookup-events --start-time 2025-11-12T14:00:00Z --end-time 2025-11-12T14:15:00Z --query 'Events' > ct-events.json

End of doc.
